To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / for negotiation purposes. Seller material treated as adversarial draft.

## Headline

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced". It (i) collapses the protection regime into a single low cap and short time limit that also captures title, tax and the specific indemnities; (ii) uses general data-room/public-register disclosure plus a constructive-knowledge clause to neutralise the warranties almost entirely; and (iii) pushes three cash items that should sit on the Seller's side of a debt-free/cash-free deal (Riverlark debt, closing bonuses, Ironquay fees) onto the Company – i.e. onto us post-Completion. Separately, the Seller Update repeatedly says matters are "addressed" or "adequate" where its own Disclosure Letter admits they are not done. Use that inconsistency.

Quantified pre-Completion items the Seller is trying to leave inside the Company:

| Item | Amount | Seller position | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3,200,000 | Release "following Completion" | Repay and release **at** Completion from price |
| DD-005 closing bonuses | AUD 420,000 + super/payroll tax/on-costs (~AUD 480–500k) | "Matter for Seller", not in funds flow | Transaction cost – deducted from price / paid via funds flow |
| Ironquay SOW3 fees | AUD 180,000 | Indemnity limited to payment | Paid pre-Completion + confirmatory assignment as CP |
| Sandbar renewals | AUD 330,000 (3 × 110k) | "Ordinary course" | Investigate; treat as leakage/working-capital item if not accrued |
| DD-006 data incident | Unquantified | "Not expected to be material" | Specific uncapped indemnity + pre-Completion assessment |
| Bluefen (30% revenue, ~AUD 3.6m) | Revenue risk | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours | Hard CP: unconditional consent + clause 11.3 conditions satisfied |

---

## 1. Liability regime (cl 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

**1.1 Fundamental/title warranties capped and time-limited as general warranties.** Reject outright. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Market position (and the minimum we should accept): title, capacity and authority warranties capped at 100% of price, claims period 6–7 years (limitation period). If title fails, the 20% cap means we pay AUD 24m and recover AUD 4.8m.

**1.2 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" / limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature".** This inverts normal drafting and would sweep in: specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, tax), completion-accounts/leakage adjustments, breach of covenant, and fraud. Require:
- Caps, thresholds and time bars apply **only** to general Warranty Claims.
- Express carve-outs: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment by Seller or its officers; specific indemnities; tax indemnity; title/capacity; price adjustment and leakage; Seller's pre-Completion conduct covenants.
- Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance (cl 12.8/20.5) must not purport to exclude fraud, equitable relief (injunction/specific performance), or statutory claims that cannot be excluded (ACL s 18 misleading conduct – a purported exclusion is of doubtful effect and we should not concede it rhetorically).

**1.3 Cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m).** Low for a business with (a) a known IP ownership gap, (b) an open privacy incident and (c) revenue concentration. Push for 30–50% on general warranties, with tiered caps: tax and IP warranties at 100%. Alternative: accept 20% only if Seller funds buy-side W&I insurance at its cost or we get a retention/escrow (see 1.6).

**1.4 Thresholds.** De minimis AUD 25,000 (~0.1% of price) is tolerable but should aggregate related claims. Basket AUD 250,000 as a **deductible** ("only the excess") is not acceptable – require a **tipping** basket (first dollar recoverable once exceeded), and carve out indemnities, tax, title and known-matter claims from both thresholds.

**1.5 Time limits.** 18 months does not cover one full audited financial year post-Completion. Require: general warranties 24 months; tax 7 years (ATO amendment periods plus buffer); title/capacity 6–7 years; environmental/IP ownership at least 3 years. Notice provisions: notice within the period should suffice, with proceedings to be commenced within a further 6–9 months.

**1.6 Counterparty risk.** Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd is a holding/venture vehicle; after Completion it may have no assets beyond our purchase price. Require (a) a parent/ultimate-holder guarantee, or (b) retention/escrow of 10–15% of price for the claims period, or (c) seller-funded W&I. Without one of these, every protection above is paper.

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge (Sch 7, cl 8.3, Disclosure Letter §1)

**2.1 General disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, the accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".** This is a blanket disclosure that, on the Seller's drafting, means anything buried anywhere in the data room qualifies every warranty. Require the standard: matters are disclosed only if **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect**. Delete general disclosure of public records, or confine it to specified searches (ASIC company extract, PPSR, IP Australia, court lists) conducted on a stated date and annexed.

**2.2 Data-room cut-off is 22 September 2026; today is 4 November.** Six weeks stale. Require a bring-down: no additions to the data room after the cut-off count as disclosure unless in a signed supplemental disclosure letter delivered at least 5 business days before signing, with a Buyer walk right if new disclosures are material.

**2.3 Clause 8.3 – no claim for anything the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.** Delete. It imports constructive knowledge of a diligence team and converts every data-room document into a warranty qualifier regardless of fairness of disclosure. If we must concede anything: limited to **actual** knowledge of three named Wattlebridge individuals of a matter that they knew would give rise to a warranty claim, and expressly excluding adviser knowledge and constructive/imputed knowledge. Add a clause that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation made by or on its behalf (the standard "no diminution by investigation" clause).

**2.4 §1.4 non-admission.** Acceptable as drafted, but pair it with an express statement in the SPA that the Disclosure Letter does not qualify the specific indemnities or the title/capacity warranties.

## 3. Bluefen change-of-control (cl 3 / 6.3; DD-002; DL §2)

Thirty percent of FY26 revenue. The Update says "addressed"; the Disclosure Letter admits no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Points:
- Consent must be a **Condition Precedent for the Buyer's benefit** (waivable only by us), not treated as satisfied merely "on delivery of written consent". The CP must require (i) unconditional written consent in a form approved by the Buyer, (ii) evidence that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied or waived by Bluefen, and (iii) no amendment to the Bluefen contract or pricing as a condition of consent without Buyer approval.
- Seller obligation: "all reasonable endeavours" with a specific obligation to procure, bear any consent cost, and keep us informed; Buyer to be involved in Bluefen communications.
- Long-stop date and Buyer termination right; consider a price adjustment or earn-out/retention mechanism if Bluefen consents subject to a reduced term or volume.
- Ask what the cl 11.3 conditions actually are – if they include a step-in, re-tender or termination right on change of control, that goes to valuation.

## 4. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DD-003; DL §3)

A release "to be provided following Completion" is incompatible with debt-free/cash-free and with cl 8.1 (change-of-control is an event of default on Completion). On the Seller's drafting we would complete into a defaulted AUD 3.2m facility with security still registered. Require:
- Payoff letter from Riverlark delivered pre-Completion stating the payout figure to Completion date.
- Funds flow directs that amount from the purchase price to Riverlark **at** Completion.
- Completion deliverables: executed deed of release/discharge, PPSR discharge (or undertaking to register release within 2 business days with a Seller indemnity), release of any guarantees given by the Company or its subsidiaries, and release of any **share mortgage over the Paperbark shares** (which also goes to title – see §9).
- Any break costs, discharge fees or default interest are Seller's cost (Debt item).

## 5. Closing bonuses (DD-005; funds flow; DL §5)

AUD 420,000 of bonuses conditional on Completion are transaction costs. "A matter for the Seller" is meaningless if the Company is the employer and pays after Completion – we fund it. Require:
- Bonuses, plus superannuation guarantee, payroll tax, and any workers' comp/other on-costs, grossed up, treated as **Transaction Expenses/Debt** in the price adjustment, or paid at Completion through the funds flow with Seller bearing them.
- Because of the continued-employment condition, some may fall due after Completion; add a specific indemnity for any amount the Company pays after Completion under DD-005.
- Confirm whether any bonuses are change-of-control payments to key staff that could trigger termination-benefit rules (Corporations Act Pt 2D.2) if any recipients are directors/KMP.

## 6. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004; DD-010; DL §4)

Under cl 7.3 the SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid; AUD 180,000 is open; no receipt or assignment in the data room. For an analytics business, unowned deliverables may sit in the product. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the wrong loss – the exposure is inability to use/licence the materials, third-party claims and remediation cost. Require:
- CP/Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment (bank confirmation, not the Seller's ledger) **and** a confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay of all SOW1–3 materials, with moral-rights consents.
- Clean IP ownership warranty (all IP used in the business owned or validly licensed), at a 100% cap, 3+ years.
- Specific indemnity for any loss arising from Ironquay/SOW materials, not limited to the fee and outside the basket/cap.
- Diligence ask: identify which product components incorporate SOW3 materials.

## 7. DD-006 data export incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL §6)

~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external address; investigation "preliminary" six weeks after the event. Under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days and, if serious harm is likely, notify OAIC and affected individuals. The notification obligation will fall on the Company – i.e. us – post-Completion, and penalties for serious/repeated interferences are now substantial (up to the greater of AUD 50m / 3× benefit / 30% turnover). "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's view with no analysis behind it. Require:
- Pre-signing: completed assessment, forensic report (was the link accessed? has the recipient confirmed deletion?), legal advice on notifiability, and any customer-contract notification obligations (check Bluefen and Mossvale contracts – a breach-notification clause there can compound the Bluefen consent risk).
- Covenant: Seller to complete assessment and make any required notifications pre-Completion, in consultation with Buyer.
- Specific indemnity for all loss, regulatory penalties, notification/remediation costs and third-party claims arising from the incident – outside de minimis/basket, separate cap (or uncapped), 6-year period.
- Warranty on Privacy Act compliance and absence of other incidents; data-handling diligence (why was an export link generated to an external address?).

## 8. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL §8)

Three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110,000 each totalling AUD 330,000, with the Seller itself saying "read together for timing/scope". The splitting pattern suggests either a materiality/authority threshold being stepped around or a single AUD 330k commitment presented as three small ones. Ask: when were they signed, by whom, under what authority, and are they terminable? If the commitments were entered pre-Completion but the cost falls post-Completion and is not in working capital/the accounts, treat as leakage or a Debt-like item. Add a pre-Completion conduct covenant requiring Buyer consent for any commitment >AUD 50,000 (and aggregated related commitments).

## 9. Title (DD-012; DL §10)

A share register entry is evidence, not proof. The Seller expressly says it does not warrant we have verified it. Our own checks before signing: ASIC current extract (members, share structure, charges), PPSR search against Paperbark and against Harbourglass (Riverlark almost certainly holds a general security deed and may hold a **share mortgage** over the Paperbark shares), the Company constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag), share certificates, and any options/convertible notes/ESOP (venture-backed company – check). SPA: unlimited, 100%-capped title and capacity warranties (see 1.1), Completion deliverables of executed transfers, certificates, register updates, director/secretary resignations and releases of any security over the shares.

## 10. Smaller points

- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation – require the Seller to give the notice pre-Completion and deliver a copy; warranty that no consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment is not a change-of-control clause on the Seller's reading; verify the drafting ourselves (some "assignment" clauses include change of control by definition). If not triggered, a warranty to that effect suffices.
- **Tax:** reject "settled under the general regime". Standard Australian position is a separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, straddle period, CGT/GST on the transaction structure, tax consolidation exit if applicable, R&D tax incentive claw-backs – likely relevant for an analytics company), capped at price, 7 years, outside basket/de minimis.
- **Disclosure Letter §11:** acceptable – but it confirms the Seller's own view that we should not rely on the Update's characterisations. Quote it back when rejecting "addressed"/"adequate"/"not material".

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Rewrite cl 12/13:** limitations apply to general Warranty Claims only; fundamental/title at 100% and 6–7 years; tax indemnity 7 years; general cap raised to 30–50% (or 20% with seller-funded W&I); tipping basket; 24-month general period; carve-outs for fraud, indemnities, leakage, covenants.
2. **Delete cl 8.3**; replace general data-room/public-record disclosure with a "fairly disclosed" standard and specified searches; bring the disclosure date down to signing with a Buyer walk right.
3. **Bluefen:** Buyer-only CP requiring unconditional consent and satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions; long-stop and termination right.
4. **Riverlark:** repay from price and deliver release/PPSR discharge/share-mortgage release **at** Completion.
5. **Bonuses, Ironquay fees, Sandbar renewals:** into the funds flow/price adjustment as Seller costs; specific indemnities for post-Completion payments.
6. **Ironquay:** payment evidence plus confirmatory assignment as CP; broad IP indemnity and 100%-capped IP warranty.
7. **DD-006:** completed assessment and any notifications pre-Completion; stand-alone uncapped indemnity.
8. **Counterparty credit:** parent guarantee or 10–15% retention/escrow – non-negotiable given Seller is an SPV.
9. **Title:** run our own ASIC/PPSR/constitution checks now; do not rely on DD-012.
10. **Negotiating posture:** lead with the gap between the Seller Update and its own Disclosure Letter – every "addressed/adequate/not material" is contradicted in the letter. That contradiction is our strongest lever for the specific indemnities and the completion mechanics.

Happy to turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up of the SPA and a Buyer issues list for the Seller if you send through the current draft.

- Confirm whether any bonuses are change-of-control payments to key staff that could trigger termination-benefit rules (Corporations Act Pt 2D.2) if any recipients are directors/KMP.

## 6. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DD-004; DD-010; DL §4)

Under cl 7.3 the SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is paid; AUD 180,000 is open; no receipt or assignment in the data room. For an analytics business, unowned deliverables may sit in the product. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the wrong loss – the exposure is inability to use/licence the materials, third-party claims and remediation cost. Require:
- CP/Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment (bank confirmation, not the Seller's ledger) **and** a confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay of all SOW1–3 materials, with moral-rights consents.
- Clean IP ownership warranty (all IP used in the business owned or validly licensed), at a 100% cap, 3+ years.
- Specific indemnity for any loss arising from Ironquay/SOW materials, not limited to the fee and outside the basket/cap.
- Diligence ask: identify which product components incorporate SOW3 materials.

## 7. DD-006 data export incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL §6)

~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external address; investigation "preliminary" six weeks after the event. Under the Privacy Act 1988 Notifiable Data Breaches scheme an entity must assess a suspected eligible data breach within 30 days and, if serious harm is likely, notify OAIC and affected individuals. The notification obligation will fall on the Company – i.e. us – post-Completion, and penalties for serious/repeated interferences are now substantial (up to the greater of AUD 50m / 3× benefit / 30% turnover). "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's view with no analysis behind it. Require:
- Pre-signing: completed assessment, forensic report (was the link accessed? has the recipient confirmed deletion?), legal advice on notifiability, and any customer-contract notification obligations (check Bluefen and Mossvale contracts – a breach-notification clause there can compound the Bluefen consent risk).
- Covenant: Seller to complete assessment and make any required notifications pre-Completion, in consultation with Buyer.
- Specific indemnity for all loss, regulatory penalties, notification/remediation costs and third-party claims arising from the incident – outside de minimis/basket, separate cap (or uncapped), 6-year period.
- Warranty on Privacy Act compliance and absence of other incidents; data-handling diligence (why was an export link generated to an external address?).

## 8. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011; DL §8)

Three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110,000 each totalling AUD 330,000, with the Seller itself saying "read together for timing/scope". The splitting pattern suggests either a materiality/authority threshold being stepped around or a single AUD 330k commitment presented as three small ones. Ask: when were they signed, by whom, under what authority, and are they terminable? If the commitments were entered pre-Completion but the cost falls post-Completion and is not in working capital/the accounts, treat as leakage or a Debt-like item. Add a pre-Completion conduct covenant requiring Buyer consent for any commitment >AUD 50,000 (and aggregated related commitments).

## 9. Title (DD-012; DL §10)

A share register entry is evidence, not proof. The Seller expressly says it does not warrant we have verified it. Our own checks before signing: ASIC current extract (members, share structure, charges), PPSR search against Paperbark and against Harbourglass (Riverlark almost certainly holds a general security deed and may hold a **share mortgage** over the Paperbark shares), the Company constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag), share certificates, and any options/convertible notes/ESOP (venture-backed company – check). SPA: unlimited, 100%-capped title and capacity warranties (see 1.1), Completion deliverables of executed transfers, certificates, register updates, director/secretary resignations and releases of any security over the shares.

## 10. Smaller points

- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification obligation – require the Seller to give the notice pre-Completion and deliver a copy; warranty that no consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** restriction on assignment is not a change-of-control clause on the Seller's reading; verify the drafting ourselves (some "assignment" clauses include change of control by definition). If not triggered, a warranty to that effect suffices.
- **Tax:** reject "settled under the general regime". Standard Australian position is a separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, straddle period, CGT/GST on the transaction structure, tax consolidation exit if applicable, R&D tax incentive claw-backs – likely relevant for an analytics company), capped at price, 7 years, outside basket/de minimis.
- **Disclosure Letter §11:** acceptable – but it confirms the Seller's own view that we should not rely on the Update's characterisations. Quote it back when rejecting "addressed"/"adequate"/"not material".

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Rewrite cl 12/13:** limitations apply to general Warranty Claims only; fundamental/title at 100% and 6–7 years; tax indemnity 7 years; general cap raised to 30–50% (or 20% with seller-funded W&I); tipping basket; 24-month general period; carve-outs for fraud, indemnities, leakage, covenants.
2. **Delete cl 8.3**; replace general data-room/public-record disclosure with a "fairly disclosed" standard and specified searches; bring the disclosure date down to signing with a Buyer walk right.
3. **Bluefen:** Buyer-only CP requiring unconditional consent and satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions; long-stop and termination right.
4. **Riverlark:** repay from price and deliver release/PPSR discharge/share-mortgage release **at** Completion.
5. **Bonuses, Ironquay fees, Sandbar renewals:** into the funds flow/price adjustment as Seller costs; specific indemnities for post-Completion payments.
6. **Ironquay:** payment evidence plus confirmatory assignment as CP; broad IP indemnity and 100%-capped IP warranty.
7. **DD-006:** completed assessment and any notifications pre-Completion; stand-alone uncapped indemnity.
8. **Counterparty credit:** parent guarantee or 10–15% retention/escrow – non-negotiable given Seller is an SPV.
9. **Title:** run our own ASIC/PPSR/constitution checks now; do not rely on DD-012.
10. **Negotiating posture:** lead with the gap between the Seller Update and its own Disclosure Letter – every "addressed/adequate/not material" is contradicted in the letter. That contradiction is our strongest lever for the specific indemnities and the completion mechanics.

Happy to turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up of the SPA and a Buyer issues list for the Seller if you send through the current draft.
